rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the same central ground-truth concern (mtp seed reproducibility lost under full cudagraphs, tied to gcanlin's follow-up note) and both raise the benchmark-attribution issue Sy0307/amy-why-3459 debated. Y goes further: its fix for the seed issue explicitly obsoletes the need for the model to read cudagraph_mode at all, directly resolving gcanlin's original 'why does modeling need cudagraph_mode' objection rather than just restating it, and its NPU point (talker_mtp_graph_safe=True is false on NPU, only papered over by the yaml pin) supplies the actual root cause behind Wallbreazzz's crash report rather than just noting the yaml exists. X's review is thorough and well-grounded (specific file:line citations throughout) but pads its output with large blocks of internal 'claim-verified/refuted' scratch notes that aren't actionable review comments, hurting signal-to-noise versus Y's tight, numbered, suggested-fix format that reads like real inline PR comments. Neither includes a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
